title: Stronger process boundaries on Linux and Windows
text: Coding agents start background processes such as dev servers, watchers and test runs, and Obeya has to stop them when a session ends. Today it tracks them by sampling the process tree, which misses a process that detaches quickly and keeps nothing running if Obeya itself crashes. We measured two operating-system boundaries with a real Codex agent: a systemd user scope per session on Linux and a Job Object per session on Windows. Both catch what sampling misses, and on Windows the boundary also ends everything when Obeya dies. Neither is in Obeya yet; the page shows what they hold, what still gets out, and what was not tested.
